title: The derived exchange transformation commutes with shifts and maps triangles to morphisms of triangles
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and let $\Ex_\square:\Phi:=g^{-1}Rf_*\to\Psi:=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ be the derived exchange transformation of functors $\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Write $[1]$ for the shift of complexes, $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$. Give each of the four functors $u^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and $Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] its shift-commutation isomorphism: for $u^{-1}$ the identity $u^{-1}(M[1])=(u^{-1}M)[1]$ of termwise shifted complexes; for $Ru_*$ the isomorphism $Ru_*(K[1])\cong u_*(I(K)[1])=(u_*I(K))[1]$ obtained by comparing the K-injective resolution $K[1]\to I(K[1])$ with the K-injective resolution $K[1]\to I(K)[1]$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Let $\xi_K:\Phi(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(K)[1]$ and $\zeta_K:\Psi(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi(K)[1]$ be the composite shift-commutation isomorphisms, and $\xi^{(n)}_K:\Phi(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(K)[n]$, $\zeta^{(n)}_K$ ($n\in\mathbf Z$) their iterates (for $n<0$ the inverses of the iterates at $K[n]$). Then:

(1) for every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, $\zeta_K\circ\Ex_{\square,K[1]}=\Ex_{\square,K}[1]\circ\xi_K$; hence $\zeta^{(n)}_K\circ\Ex_{\square,K[n]}=\Ex_{\square,K}[n]\circ\xi^{(n)}_K$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$;

(2) for every triangle $X_1\xrightarrow{u}X_2\xrightarrow{v}X_3\xrightarrow{w}X_1[1]$ in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], the triple $(\Ex_{\square,X_1},\Ex_{\square,X_2},\Ex_{\square,X_3})$ is a morphism of triangles from $(\Phi X_1,\Phi X_2,\Phi X_3,\Phi u,\Phi v,\xi_{X_1}\circ\Phi w)$ to $(\Psi X_1,\Psi X_2,\Psi X_3,\Psi u,\Psi v,\zeta_{X_1}\circ\Psi w)$.

(Part (2) follows from (1) and the naturality of $\Ex_\square$; part (1) says that $\Ex_\square$ is a morphism of triangulated functors.)

mathlib_searches.results: NatTrans.CommShift (a natural transformation commuting with the shift isomorphisms, CommShift.lean:346) with instances id, comp, whiskerLeft, whiskerRight, of_iso_inv (lines 389-422)
mathlib_searches.verdict: generalization of the notion, not of the statement: Mathlib has the notion used in (1) and its stability under composition and whiskering, but nothing about etale sheaves, the derived inverse and direct images, or the exchange transformation

mathlib_searches.results: Adjunction.CommShift (unit and counit commute with shifts, Adjunction.lean:208), rightAdjointCommShift (Adjunction.lean:388, the right adjoint of a CommShift functor gets a CommShift structure, Stacks 0A8D); the only file mentioning both mates/conjugates and CommShift is Shift/Adjunction.lean, which has no statement that the mate of a CommShift transformation is CommShift
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: the tools for a proof are there (the exchange transformation is unit, then theta, then counit, whiskered; each commutes with shifts), the statement is not

mathlib_searches.results: Functor.mapTriangle (line 42) and mapTriangleIso (line 168): a natural isomorphism e with NatTrans.CommShift e.hom gives an isomorphism of the image triangles; no version for a non-invertible natural transformation
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match for (2) for a non-invertible transformation; the isomorphism case's proof (naturality plus the CommShift square) is the proof of (2)
